## 6. Many parameters: separability, medians and boxes

### 6.1 A separability principle

**Theorem 6.1 (Separability principle).** Let $F_1,\dots,F_d : \mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$. Then
$$\Bigl(\forall y \in \mathbb{R}^d:\ \sum_i F_i(\theta_i) \le \sum_i F_i(y_i)\Bigr) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \Bigl(\forall i,\ \forall t\in\mathbb{R}:\ F_i(\theta_i) \le F_i(t)\Bigr).$$

*Proof sketch.* ($\Rightarrow$) Given $i$ and $t$, compare $\theta$ with the vector that agrees with $\theta$ except in coordinate $i$ where it takes the value $t$; all terms $j \ne i$ cancel, leaving $F_i(\theta_i)\le F_i(t)$. ($\Leftarrow$) Sum the coordinatewise inequalities. $\square$

Elementary as it is, this is the exact statement needed to lift every scalar result to $d$ parameters *without loss*, and it is the loss-side shadow of the fact that the dynamics also factors coordinatewise.

### 6.2 Odd samples in $d$ coordinates

**Definition 6.2.** For $k \in \mathbb{N}^d$ and samples $x^{(1)},\dots,x^{(d)}$, the separable loss and coordinatewise median are
$$L^{\mathrm{sep}}(\theta) := \sum_{i=1}^d L_{2k_i+1}\bigl(x^{(i)};\theta_i\bigr), \qquad m_i := x^{(i)}_{k_i};$$
simultaneous clipped descent is $V_\eta(\theta)_i := \Phi_{m_i,\eta}(\theta_i)$.

**Theorem 6.3.** If each $x^{(i)}$ is sorted up to $2k_i+1$, then
$$L^{\mathrm{sep}}(m) + \sum_i |\theta_i - m_i| \le L^{\mathrm{sep}}(\theta),$$
and $\theta$ minimizes $L^{\mathrm{sep}}$ if and only if $\theta = m$.

*Proof sketch.* Sum Theorem 3.1 over coordinates; for uniqueness, a vanishing sum of nonnegative terms has all terms zero. $\square$

**Theorem 6.4 (Vector termination time).** For $\eta>0$, $V_\eta^{\,n}(\theta) = m$ if and only if $|\theta_i - m_i| \le n\eta$ for all $i$. Consequently, with $N := \max_i \lceil |\theta_i - m_i|/\eta\rceil$, we have $V_\eta^{\,N}(\theta) = m$ and $V_\eta^{\,n}(\theta) \ne m$ for all $n<N$.

*Proof sketch.* Iterates act coordinatewise, so this is Theorem 3.4 applied in each coordinate; the maximum over coordinates of the scalar stopping times is the vector stopping time, and if $n$ is below the maximum then some coordinate has not yet arrived, by the scalar lower bound of Theorem 3.5. $\square$

Thus the *slowest coordinate sets the clock*, exactly.

### 6.3 Even samples in $d$ coordinates: the minimizer box

**Definition 6.5.** For even samples, $L^{\mathrm{box}}(\theta) := \sum_{i=1}^d L_{2k_i+2}(x^{(i)};\theta_i)$, with corners $\ell_i := x^{(i)}_{k_i}$, $h_i := x^{(i)}_{k_i+1}$, and the simultaneous interval update $B_\eta(\theta)_i := S_{\ell_i,h_i,\eta}(\theta_i)$.

**Theorem 6.6 (The minimizer set is a box).** If each $x^{(i)}$ is sorted up to $2k_i+2$, then $\theta$ minimizes $L^{\mathrm{box}}$ if and only if
$$\theta \in \prod_{i=1}^{d} \bigl[\ell_i,\ h_i\bigr].$$

*Proof sketch.* Theorem 6.1 reduces global minimality to coordinatewise minimality; Theorem 4.3 identifies each coordinate's minimizer set as $[\ell_i,h_i]$. $\square$

**Theorem 6.7 (Box descent terminates at the projection).** Let $\eta>0$ and $\ell_i \le h_i$ for all $i$. Then for all
$$n \;\ge\; \max_{i} \Bigl\lceil \bigl|\theta_i - \pi_{\ell_i,h_i}(\theta_i)\bigr|/\eta \Bigr\rceil,$$
we have $B_\eta^{\,n}(\theta) = \bigl(\pi_{\ell_i,h_i}(\theta_i)\bigr)_{i=1}^d$, the metric projection of $\theta$ onto the box.

*Proof sketch.* Iterates act coordinatewise (immediate induction), so apply Theorem 4.7 in each coordinate; membership of $n$ above the maximum of the ceilings gives $n\eta \ge |\theta_i - \pi_i(\theta_i)|$ for every $i$. $\square$

**Theorem 6.8 (Even-sample vector training theorem).** Under the hypotheses of Theorems 6.6 and 6.7, there exists $N$ such that for all $n \ge N$, the $n$-th iterate of simultaneous clipped descent equals the projection of the initialization onto the minimizer box *and* is an exact minimizer of $L^{\mathrm{box}}$.

*Proof sketch.* Combine Theorem 6.7 (the iterate is the projection) with Theorem 6.6 (the projection lies in the box, hence is optimal). $\square$

**Example 6.9.** Two coordinates with four-point samples $(-3,-1,2,5)$ and $(0,1,1,4)$ give the minimizer box $[-1,2]\times[1,1]$: a segment in the first coordinate, a degenerate point in the second (its two central order statistics coincide). Descent from any initialization lands on the nearest point of this box in finitely many steps.

---

## 7. Exact ReLU width of the training step

We now turn from dynamics to expressivity. Since every map considered is continuous piecewise linear, each *is* a small ReLU network; the question is how small, and the answer turns out to encode the minimizer geometry.

**Definition 7.1 (Width-$k$ network with affine skip).** For $a,b,c \in \mathbb{R}^k$ and $p,q \in \mathbb{R}$,
$$N_{a,b,c,p,q}(x) := \sum_{j=1}^{k} a_j\,\mathrm{relu}(b_j x + c_j) \;+\; px + q .$$

The affine skip term $px+q$ is included deliberately: lower bounds that survive it are considerably stronger, since a linear bypass can absorb global slope for free.

### 7.1 The curvature test

**Lemma 7.2 (A rectified unit is flat off its kink).** If $|v| \le |u|$ then $\mathrm{relu}(u+v)+\mathrm{relu}(u-v)-2\,\mathrm{relu}(u) = 0$.

*Proof sketch.* If $u \ge 0$ then $u\pm v \ge 0$ and all three rectifications are the identity; if $u \le 0$ then $u \pm v \le 0$ and all three vanish. $\square$

**Theorem 7.3 (Networks are affine off all kinks).** Let $h \ge 0$ and suppose $|b_j|\,h \le |b_j x + c_j|$ for every $j$ (no unit's kink lies strictly inside the window of radius $h$ at $x$). Then
$$N(x+h) + N(x-h) - 2N(x) = 0 .$$

*Proof sketch.* Apply Lemma 7.2 to each unit with $u = b_jx+c_j$, $v = b_jh$; the skip term $px+q$ has vanishing second difference identically. $\square$

**Corollary 7.4 (Kink-witness principle).** If $h \ge 0$ and $N(x+h)+N(x-h)-2N(x) \ne 0$, then some unit $j$ satisfies $|b_j x + c_j| < |b_j|\,h$, i.e. its kink $-c_j/b_j$ lies strictly inside $(x-h, x+h)$.

This is the contrapositive of Theorem 7.3, and it is remarkably cheap: it requires no convexity, no differentiability, and no sign conditions on the network parameters.

**Lemma 7.5 (Window separation).** If a single unit $(b,c)$ has its kink inside both the radius-$h$ window at $x$ and the radius-$h$ window at $y$, then $|x-y| < 2h$.

*Proof sketch.* From $|bx+c| < |b|h$ we get $b \ne 0$; then $|b|\,|x-y| = |(bx+c)-(by+c)| \le |bx+c|+|by+c| < 2|b|h$, and divide by $|b|>0$. $\square$

Corollary 7.4 plus Lemma 7.5 yields the general method: **exhibit $r$ points with pairwise distances at least $2h$ at which the target map has nonvanishing second difference over radius $h$; conclude $k \ge r$.**

### 7.2 The scalar update: width exactly two

**Theorem 7.6 (Lower bound two).** Let $t>0$. If $N_{a,b,c,p,q} = \Phi_{m,t}$ on all of $\mathbb{R}$, then $k \ge 2$.

*Proof sketch.* Take $h = t/2$. At $x = m-t$ the values of $\Phi_{m,t}$ at $x-h, x, x+h$ are $m-h, m, m$, so the second difference is $(m)+(m-h)-2m = -h \ne 0$. At $x = m+t$ they are $m, m, m+h$, giving second difference $h \ne 0$. The two centers are $2t = 4h \ge 2h$ apart, so by Corollary 7.4 and Lemma 7.5 the two witnessing units are distinct. $\square$

**Theorem 7.7 (Two units suffice).** For $t \ge 0$ and all $x$,
$$\Phi_{m,t}(x) = m + \mathrm{relu}(x-m-t) - \mathrm{relu}(m-x-t).$$
Equivalently $\Phi_{m,t} = N_{a,b,c,0,m}$ with $a = (1,-1)$, $b=(1,-1)$, $c = (-(m+t),\,m-t)$.

**Theorem 7.8 (Exact width two).** For $t>0$ the clipped tropical update is realized by a width-two network and by no narrower one, even allowing an arbitrary affine skip.

A complementary, weaker argument is also available and instructive: a single unit $x\mapsto a\,\mathrm{relu}(bx+c)+e$ is convex (if $a\ge0$) or concave (if $a\le0$), whereas $\Phi_{m,t}$ rises, is flat on $[m-t,m+t]$, and rises again — so it is neither. Formally, midpoint convexity of $\mathrm{relu}$ contradicts the sampled values at $m-2t, m-t, m$ in the convex case and at $m, m+t, m+2t$ in the concave case. This argument does not survive the addition of a skip term; the curvature method does.

### 7.3 The interval update: width exactly four

**Theorem 7.9 (Explicit four-unit form).** For $\ell \le h$ and $\eta \ge 0$, for all $\theta$,
$$S_{\ell,h,\eta}(\theta) = \theta + \eta - \mathrm{relu}\bigl(\theta - (\ell-\eta)\bigr) + \mathrm{relu}(\theta-\ell) - \mathrm{relu}(\theta - h) + \mathrm{relu}\bigl(\theta - (h+\eta)\bigr).$$

*Proof sketch.* Five regions, delimited by the four kinks $\ell-\eta < \ell \le h < h+\eta$. On each region, evaluate the update via its explicit piecewise form — $S(\theta) = \min(\ell, \theta+\eta)$ for $\theta \le \ell$, $S(\theta)=\theta$ for $\theta\in[\ell,h]$, $S(\theta)=\max(h,\theta-\eta)$ for $\theta \ge h$ — and evaluate each rectification as either $0$ or its argument. Each of the five identities is then a polynomial identity. $\square$

**Theorem 7.10 (Lower bound four).** Let $\ell<h$ and $\eta>0$. If $N_{a,b,c,p,q} = S_{\ell,h,\eta}$ on all of $\mathbb{R}$, then $k \ge 4$.

*Proof sketch.* Take $h_0 := \min(\eta,\,h-\ell)/2 > 0$, so that consecutive kinks among $\ell-\eta<\ell<h<h+\eta$ are at least $2h_0$ apart. Evaluate $S$ at the twelve points $c \pm h_0, c$ for $c \in \{\ell-\eta,\ \ell,\ h,\ h+\eta\}$:
at $\ell-\eta$ the values are $(\ell-h_0,\ \ell,\ \ell)$, second difference $+h_0$;
at $\ell$: $(\ell,\ \ell,\ \ell+h_0)$, second difference $+h_0$;
at $h$: $(h-h_0,\ h,\ h)$, second difference $-h_0$;
at $h+\eta$: $(h,\ h,\ h+h_0)$, second difference $+h_0$.
All four are nonzero, so Corollary 7.4 produces four witnessing units, pairwise distinct by Lemma 7.5 since the four centers are pairwise at least $2h_0$ apart. A set of four distinct indices in $\{1,\dots,k\}$ forces $k\ge4$. $\square$

**Theorem 7.11 (Exact width four).** For $\ell<h$, $\eta>0$: four units with an affine skip realize $S_{\ell,h,\eta}$ exactly (Theorem 7.9, with $a = (-1,1,-1,1)$, $b=(1,1,1,1)$, $c = (\eta-\ell,\,-\ell,\,-h,\,-(h+\eta))$, $p=1$, $q=\eta$), and no network of fewer units can.

### 7.4 The width dichotomy

The degenerate case unifies the two parities.

**Lemma 7.12.** $S_{m,m,\eta} = \Phi_{m,\eta}$: a degenerate interval reproduces the scalar clipped update.

**Theorem 7.13 (Width dichotomy).** Let $\ell \le h$ and $\eta>0$. One clipped descent step toward the tropical $L^1$ minimizer set $[\ell,h]$ has exact ReLU width (with an arbitrary affine skip permitted)
$$\mathrm{width}\bigl(S_{\ell,h,\eta}\bigr) = \begin{cases} 2, & \ell = h \ \ (\text{minimizer set is a point}),\\ 4, & \ell < h \ \ (\text{minimizer set is a nondegenerate segment}).\end{cases}$$

*Proof sketch.* If $\ell=h$, Lemma 7.12 and Theorem 7.8. If $\ell<h$, Theorem 7.11. $\square$

Since the parity of the sample size decides whether the minimizer set is a point or a segment (Corollary 3.2 versus Theorem 4.3), Theorem 7.13 says the minimal architecture implementing one training step *detects the parity structure of the data*. The width is an invariant of the tropical minimizer geometry, not an artifact of the particular formula used to write the update.

---

## 8. Algorithms

Three procedures summarize the constructive content.

**Algorithm A (Exact tropical training, odd samples).**
Given sorted reduced samples $x_0\le\cdots\le x_{2k}$, initialization $\theta_0$, step $\eta>0$:
compute $m := x_k$; compute $N := \lceil |\theta_0-m|/\eta\rceil$; return $m$ and $N$.
By Theorem 3.5 this is exactly what the iteration would produce, at exactly the step it would produce it. Cost: $O(n)$ after sorting (or $O(n)$ total via linear-time selection), versus $O(N)$ for naive iteration.

**Algorithm B (Exact tropical training, even samples / boxes).**
Given per-coordinate sorted samples of even sizes $2k_i+2$: set $\ell_i := x^{(i)}_{k_i}$, $h_i := x^{(i)}_{k_i+1}$; return the box $\prod_i[\ell_i,h_i]$, the projection $\theta^\star_i = \max(\ell_i,\min(h_i,\theta_{0,i}))$, and the stopping time $N = \max_i\lceil|\theta_{0,i}-\theta^\star_i|/\eta\rceil$. Justified by Theorems 6.6–6.8. Cost $O(\sum_i n_i)$ after sorting.

**Algorithm C (Width-optimal ReLU compilation of a training step).**
Given $\ell\le h$ and $\eta>0$: if $\ell=h$ emit the two-unit network of Theorem 7.7; else emit the four-unit network of Theorem 7.9. By Theorem 7.13 the emitted width is minimal.

---

## 9. Discussion

**Why everything is exact.** Three structural facts conspire. First, the loss is piecewise affine with integer slopes given by block imbalances (Theorems 2.1–2.3), so its minimizer set is a face of a subdivision — a vertex in the odd case, an edge in the even case. Second, the clipped update is a genuine one-parameter semigroup (Proposition 1.5), so iteration is time-reparametrization rather than approximation; there is no step-size restriction and no discretization error at any $\eta>0$. Third, the distance-to-target law is an identity (Proposition 1.4) rather than a contraction estimate, which is why both the upper bound *and* the matching lower bound on the stopping time come out for free.

**Comparison with classical subgradient theory.** For a general convex nonsmooth objective, subgradient descent with a fixed step converges only to an $O(\eta)$-neighbourhood of the optimum, and the standard rate is $O(1/\sqrt{n})$ in function value. Here, by contrast, the clipping makes the optimum an exact fixed point, and the theory delivers finite termination at an exact optimum for *every* positive step. Theorem 5.6 shows this is exactly as fragile as one would expect and no more: under $\varepsilon$-noise, the guarantee degrades to a terminal radius of exactly $\varepsilon$ and an effective speed of exactly $\eta-\varepsilon$.

**The role of parity.** Sample parity is usually a footnote in median estimation. In the tropical setting it becomes structural: it determines whether the argmin is $0$- or $1$-dimensional, whether the terminal parameter is initialization-independent or initialization-selected, and — via Theorem 7.13 — the exact width of the smallest network that computes the training step. The odd case has a unique optimum and a canonical answer; the even case has an optimal face and the algorithm performs an implicit *minimum-norm-change* selection on it.

**Kink counting as a width method.** Corollary 7.4 with Lemma 7.5 is a general-purpose lower-bound technique for shallow rectified networks representing a CPL map: any $r$ pairwise $2h$-separated points with nonvanishing radius-$h$ second difference force width $\ge r$. It is immune to affine skip connections and requires no global shape hypothesis. The two instances proved here, $r = 2$ and $r=4$, are the two smallest, and both are tight.

---

## 10. Future directions

**1. Width equals the number of curvature sites.** Conjecture: if $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is continuous piecewise linear with exactly $r$ kinks, then the minimal width $k$ for which $f = N_{a,b,c,p,q}$ is exactly $r$. The kink-witness principle already converts a nonvanishing second difference into a *distinct* unit whenever the test windows are disjoint, so the lower bound $r \le k$ needs no convexity, differentiability, or sign pattern — only separation of kinks; the matching upper bound should follow from the telescoping construction used in Theorem 7.9. The two smallest instances ($r=2$ and $r=4$) are proved here by the same mechanism, and the dichotomy of Theorem 7.13 shows the width is a genuine invariant of the tropical minimizer geometry rather than an artifact of the formula.

**2. Tropical width spectrum of $d$-dimensional box descent.** Conjecture: for the separable box update on $d$ coordinates with $s := \#\{i : \ell_i < h_i\}$ nondegenerate coordinates, the total rectified width required to implement one simultaneous step as a map $\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ built from scalar units with arbitrary affine skips is exactly $2d + 2s$. Separability makes the curvature test coordinatewise — the separability principle is the loss-side shadow of the same phenomenon — so the widths should add: $2$ per degenerate coordinate and $4$ per nondegenerate one. The $d$-dimensional dynamics is already known to factor exactly through the $d$ scalar ones, and the scalar widths $2$ and $4$ are theorems, so the only missing ingredient is the $d$-dimensional counting argument.

**3. Perturbed descent has a sharp asymptotic radius equal to $\varepsilon$.** Conjecture: for every $0\le\varepsilon<\eta$ and every $\varepsilon$-perturbed trajectory, $\limsup_n |u_n - m| \le \varepsilon$, with equality attained by some trajectory, so that the supremum over trajectories of $\limsup_n|u_n-m|$ equals $\varepsilon$; moreover the loss excess satisfies $\limsup_n\bigl(L(u_n)-L(m)\bigr) = n_{\text{samples}}\cdot\varepsilon$ for a sample whose median has full one-sided multiplicity.

**4. Odd-sample extension in full generality.** For every odd sample size $2k+1$, clipped unit-step subgradient descent on the scalar tropical $L^1$ empirical loss reaches the unique sample median after at most $\lceil|\theta_0-m|/\eta\rceil$ iterations for every $\eta>0$.

**5. Vector tropical monomials.** For a separable $d$-parameter tropical affine model with coordinatewise three-point losses, simultaneous clipped descent terminates after at most the maximum of the $d$ coordinatewise termination times.

**6. Perturbed tropical limit, quantitatively.** If each tropical update is perturbed by an error of magnitude at most $\varepsilon<\eta$, then the parameter distance after $n$ steps is at most $\max\bigl(0,\ |\theta_0-m|-n(\eta-\varepsilon)\bigr)$ until the trajectory enters the closed $\varepsilon$-neighbourhood of the minimizer.

**7. Even-sample minimizer interval in the perturbed and stochastic regimes.** For $2k$ ordered scalar residual targets the tropical $L^1$ minimizers form the interval between the two central order statistics and clipped descent reaches it in finite time for every positive step size; the corresponding statements under sampling noise, and the induced distribution of the terminal point on the optimal face, remain open.

---

## 11. Conclusion

For tropical $L^1$ regression, training is not an approximation process. A single counting inequality determines the entire minimizer geometry — a point for odd samples, a segment for even ones, a product box in the separable multi-parameter setting. A semigroup identity turns iterated clipped subgradient descent into an exactly solvable flow, giving finite termination at an exact optimum with a stopping time that is simultaneously an upper and a lower bound. Noise degrades this in a completely quantified way, with a saturation radius that is attained. And the same piecewise-linear rigidity that makes the dynamics solvable makes the *architecture* of the update rule an invariant: exactly two rectified units when the optimum is a point, exactly four when it is a segment. Optimization geometry and network width, in this setting, are two readings of the same combinatorial data.

\begin{abstract}
We give a complete and exact theory of clipped subgradient descent for tropical $L^1$ regression. For a tropical monomial model with a single trainable parameter, the empirical absolute-error loss on $n$ reduced samples is $L(\theta)=\sum_{i<n}|\theta-x_i|$, and we derive all of its minimizer geometry from a single counting inequality: sliding the parameter across a pivot increases the loss at a rate equal to the imbalance between the sample blocks on the two sides, with equality on any slab crossing no data point. From this we obtain, for odd sample size $2k+1$, the growth bound $L(x_k)+|\theta-x_k|\le L(\theta)$ and hence a unique minimizer at the sample median; and, for even sample size $2k+2$, constancy of the loss on $[x_k,x_{k+1}]$ with slope at least $2$ outside, so that the minimizer set is exactly that closed interval. The clipped update is a one-parameter semigroup, so $n$ steps of size $\eta$ equal one flow of duration $n\eta$; with the exact distance identity $|\Phi_{m,t}(x)-m|=\max(0,|x-m|-t)$ this yields finite termination at the exact optimum at time $\lceil|x_0-m|/\eta\rceil$, with a matching lower bound and an explicit excess-risk rate. In the even case the metric projection onto the optimal interval is conserved by the dynamics, reducing interval descent to the scalar flow. We further prove: a sharp perturbed-descent bound $|u_n-m|\le\max(\varepsilon,|u_0-m|-n(\eta-\varepsilon))$ with attained saturation radius $\varepsilon$; a separability principle yielding a product-box minimizer set and coordinatewise termination in the maximum of the coordinatewise times; and, via a discrete curvature (kink-witness) test, exact rectified-unit widths for the training step itself: two when the optimum is a point, four when it is a nondegenerate segment, both robust to an arbitrary affine skip connection.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}

The tropical (max-plus) semiring $\mathbb{T}=(\R\cup\{-\infty\},\oplus,\otimes)$ with $a\oplus b=\max(a,b)$ and $a\otimes b=a+b$ is the algebraic home of a large family of piecewise-linear phenomena: shortest paths, scheduling, optimal control, and rectified neural networks. A network whose only nonlinearity is $\relu(x)=\max(x,0)$ computes a difference of tropical polynomials, and conversely; the two languages describe the same class of continuous piecewise-linear (CPL) maps.

This correspondence invites a question about \emph{learning} rather than representation: what does a standard optimizer do when applied to a tropical model with a natural loss? We answer this completely for the smallest nontrivial case and its multi-parameter generalizations. Every statement below is an identity or a two-sided bound with attained constants, rather than an asymptotic rate.

\subsection{The model}
A tropical monomial in one variable with a single parameter is $z\mapsto z\otimes\theta=z+\theta$. Given data $(z_j,y_j)_{j<n}$ and absolute-error loss, the $j$-th residual is $|(z_j+\theta)-y_j|=|\theta-x_j|$ with $x_j:=y_j-z_j$, the \emph{reduced samples}. The one-parameter problem is thus equivalent to $L^1$ location estimation.

\begin{definition}[Tropical $L^1$ empirical loss]
For $n\in\N$, a sample $x:\N\to\R$, and $\theta\in\R$,
\[ L_n(x;\theta):=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}|\theta-x_i|. \]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Sorted sample]
$x$ is \emph{sorted up to $n$} if $x_i\le x_j$ whenever $i\le j<n$.
\end{definition}

\subsection{The optimizer}

\begin{definition}[Clipped tropical update]
For target $m\in\R$ and time $t\ge0$,
\[
\Phi_{m,t}(x):=\begin{cases}\min(m,\ x+t), & x<m,\\ \max(m,\ x-t), & x\ge m.\end{cases}
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Exact distance law]\label{prop:dist}
$\bigl|\Phi_{m,t}(x)-m\bigr|=\max\bigl(0,|x-m|-t\bigr)$, and $\Phi_{m,t}(x)=m$ if and only if $|x-m|\le t$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Semigroup law]\label{prop:semi}
$\Phi_{m,0}=\mathrm{id}$, and $\Phi_{m,s}\circ\Phi_{m,t}=\Phi_{m,t+s}$ for $s\ge0$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Both are case analyses on the position of $x$ relative to $m$ and on which argument of $\min$/$\max$ is active; after expanding, every branch is a linear inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Discrete equals continuous]\label{cor:iter}
For $\eta\ge0$ and $n\in\N$, $\Phi_{m,\eta}^{\,n}=\Phi_{m,n\eta}$.
\end{corollary}

Corollary~\ref{cor:iter} is the structural reason the theory is exact: the discretization of the clipped flow is not an approximation of it, at any step size.

\section{The counting mechanism}

\begin{theorem}[Right-hand growth bound]\label{thm:right}
Let $j\le n$, $p\le\theta$, and suppose $x_i\le p$ for all $i<j$. Then
\[ L_n(x;p)+\bigl(j-(n-j)\bigr)(\theta-p)\ \le\ L_n(x;\theta). \]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Split $\sum_{i<n}=\sum_{i<j}+\sum_{j\le i<n}$. For $i<j$, $x_i\le p\le\theta$ gives $|\theta-x_i|=|p-x_i|+(\theta-p)$ exactly, contributing $+j(\theta-p)$. For $i\ge j$, the reverse triangle inequality gives $|\theta-x_i|\ge|p-x_i|-(\theta-p)$, contributing at least $-(n-j)(\theta-p)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Left-hand growth bound]\label{thm:left}
Let $j\le n$, $\theta\le p$, and suppose $p\le x_i$ for all $j\le i<n$. Then
\[ L_n(x;p)+\bigl((n-j)-j\bigr)(p-\theta)\ \le\ L_n(x;\theta). \]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exact slab formula]\label{thm:slab}
If in addition to the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:right} we have $\theta\le x_i$ for all $j\le i<n$, then
\[ L_n(x;\theta)=L_n(x;p)+\bigl(j-(n-j)\bigr)(\theta-p). \]
\end{theorem}

Theorem~\ref{thm:slab} is the sharpness statement behind every constant below: on a slab crossing no data point the loss is affine with slope exactly $j-(n-j)$.

\begin{proposition}[Lipschitz control]\label{prop:lip}
$\bigl|L_n(x;\theta)-L_n(x;\theta')\bigr|\le n\,|\theta-\theta'|$.
\end{proposition}

\section{Odd samples: a unique median and exact termination}

Throughout, $n=2k+1$, $x$ sorted up to $n$, and $m:=x_k$.

\begin{theorem}[Odd-sample linear growth]\label{thm:oddgrowth}
For all $\theta\in\R$, $\ L_{2k+1}(x;m)+|\theta-m|\le L_{2k+1}(x;\theta)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For $\theta\ge m$ apply Theorem~\ref{thm:right} with pivot $m$ and $j=k+1$; the coefficient is $(k+1)-k=1$. For $\theta\le m$ apply Theorem~\ref{thm:left} with $j=k$; the coefficient is again $1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Uniqueness]\label{cor:oddunique}
$\theta$ minimizes $L_{2k+1}(x;\cdot)$ if and only if $\theta=m$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Sharpness]\label{thm:oddslab}
For $m\le\theta\le x_{k+1}$, $\ L_{2k+1}(x;\theta)=L_{2k+1}(x;m)+(\theta-m)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Termination criterion]\label{thm:termcrit}
For $\eta>0$ and $n\in\N$: $\ \Phi_{m,\eta}^{\,n}(x_0)=m \iff |x_0-m|\le n\eta$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Corollary~\ref{cor:iter} the left side is $\Phi_{m,n\eta}(x_0)=m$; apply Proposition~\ref{prop:dist}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact stopping time with matching lower bound]\label{thm:stop}
For $\eta>0$ set $N:=\lceil|x_0-m|/\eta\rceil$. Then $\Phi_{m,\eta}^{\,N}(x_0)=m$, while $\Phi_{m,\eta}^{\,n}(x_0)\neq m$ for every $n<N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Odd-sample training theorem]
Let $x$ be sorted up to $2k+1$, $\eta>0$, $x_0\in\R$, $N=\lceil|x_0-x_k|/\eta\rceil$. Clipped subgradient descent reaches $x_k$ at step $N$ and at no earlier step, and $x_k$ is the unique minimizer of the tropical $L^1$ empirical loss.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Excess-risk rate]\label{thm:risk}
For $\eta\ge0$ and $\theta_n:=\Phi_{x_k,\eta}^{\,n}(x_0)$,
\[ 0\ \le\ L_{2k+1}(x;\theta_n)-L_{2k+1}(x;x_k)\ \le\ (2k+1)\max\bigl(0,\ |x_0-x_k|-n\eta\bigr). \]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Lower bound: Corollary~\ref{cor:oddunique}. Upper bound: Proposition~\ref{prop:lip} with the exact distance $|\theta_n-x_k|=\max(0,|x_0-x_k|-n\eta)$ from Propositions~\ref{prop:dist} and Corollary~\ref{cor:iter}.
\end{proof}

\begin{example}
For $x=(-3,-1,0,4,9)$: $k=2$, $m=0$, $L(0)=17$ and $L(\pm1)=18$, matching the unit slope of Theorem~\ref{thm:oddslab}. Descent from $x_0=5$ with $\eta=2$ terminates at step $\lceil5/2\rceil=3$, with iterates $5\to3\to1\to0$.
\end{example}

\section{Even samples: the minimizer set is a segment}

Throughout, $n=2k+2$, $x$ sorted up to $n$, $\ell:=x_k$, $h:=x_{k+1}$.

\begin{theorem}[Constancy on the central interval]\label{thm:evenconst}
For $\ell\le\theta\le h$,
\[ L_{2k+2}(x;\theta)=\sum_{i=k+1}^{2k+1}x_i-\sum_{i=0}^{k}x_i, \]
independent of $\theta$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Split at $k+1$: the lower block contributes $(k+1)\theta-\sum_{i\le k}x_i$ and the upper block $\sum_{i\ge k+1}x_i-(k+1)\theta$; the $\theta$-terms cancel.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Slope-two growth outside]\label{thm:evengrowth}
For $\theta\ge h$, $L(h)+2(\theta-h)\le L(\theta)$; for $\theta\le\ell$, $L(\ell)+2(\ell-\theta)\le L(\theta)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Even-sample minimizer interval]\label{thm:evenmin}
$\theta$ minimizes $L_{2k+2}(x;\cdot)$ if and only if $\theta\in[\ell,h]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}
The metric projection onto $[\ell,h]$ is $\pi_{\ell,h}(\theta):=\max(\ell,\min(h,\theta))$; the \emph{interval update} with step $\eta$ is $S_{\ell,h,\eta}(\theta):=\Phi_{\pi_{\ell,h}(\theta),\eta}(\theta)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Projection is conserved]\label{thm:proj}
For $\eta\ge0$ and $\ell\le h$: $\pi_{\ell,h}\bigl(S_{\ell,h,\eta}(\theta)\bigr)=\pi_{\ell,h}(\theta)$, hence $\pi_{\ell,h}\bigl(S^{\,n}_{\ell,h,\eta}(\theta)\bigr)=\pi_{\ell,h}(\theta)$ for all $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Closed form and exact distance]\label{thm:intclosed}
For $\eta\ge0$, $\ell\le h$, $n\in\N$,
\[ S^{\,n}_{\ell,h,\eta}(\theta)=\Phi_{\pi_{\ell,h}(\theta),\,n\eta}(\theta),\qquad
\bigl|S^{\,n}_{\ell,h,\eta}(\theta)-\pi_{\ell,h}(\theta)\bigr|=\max\bigl(0,|\theta-\pi_{\ell,h}(\theta)|-n\eta\bigr). \]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Induction on $n$, rewriting the target of the $(n{+}1)$-st step by Theorem~\ref{thm:proj} and applying Proposition~\ref{prop:semi}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Even-sample descent theorem]\label{thm:evendescent}
Let $x$ be sorted up to $2k+2$ and $\eta>0$. For every $n\ge\bigl\lceil|\theta-\pi_{\ell,h}(\theta)|/\eta\bigr\rceil$ we have $S^{\,n}_{\ell,h,\eta}(\theta)=\pi_{\ell,h}(\theta)$, and this point is an exact minimizer of the tropical $L^1$ loss.
\end{theorem}

\begin{example}
For $x=(-3,-1,2,5)$: $[\ell,h]=[-1,2]$ and $L\equiv11$ there, while $L(3)=13=11+2\cdot1$, matching Theorem~\ref{thm:evengrowth}.
\end{example}

\section{Perturbed descent: a sharp saturation radius}

\begin{definition}
A sequence $u:\N\to\R$ is \emph{$\varepsilon$-perturbed} for target $m$ and step $\eta$ if $|u_{n+1}-\Phi_{m,\eta}(u_n)|\le\varepsilon$ for all $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[One-step contraction]\label{lem:pstep}
For an $\varepsilon$-perturbed trajectory, $|u_{n+1}-m|\le\varepsilon+\max(0,|u_n-m|-\eta)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Perturbed tropical limit]\label{thm:pbound}
If $\varepsilon\le\eta$ then for all $n$,
\[ |u_n-m|\ \le\ \max\bigl(\varepsilon,\ |u_0-m|-n(\eta-\varepsilon)\bigr). \]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Induction using Lemma~\ref{lem:pstep}; the four cases arising from the two maxima are each arithmetic consequences of $\varepsilon\le\eta$. Outside the $\varepsilon$-ball the ideal step gains $\eta$ and the noise returns at most $\varepsilon$, giving net gain $\eta-\varepsilon$ per step; inside, the bound saturates at $\varepsilon$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
If $\varepsilon\le\eta$ and $|u_n-m|>\varepsilon$, then $|u_n-m|\le|u_0-m|-n(\eta-\varepsilon)$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Absorption]
If $0\le\varepsilon<\eta$ then there is $N$ with $|u_n-m|\le\varepsilon$ for all $n\ge N$; any $N>|u_0-m|/(\eta-\varepsilon)$ works.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The radius is attained]\label{thm:sharp}
For $0<\varepsilon\le\eta$, the constant sequence $u_n\equiv m+\varepsilon$ is an $\varepsilon$-perturbed trajectory with $|u_n-m|=\varepsilon$ for all $n$. Consequently Theorem~\ref{thm:pbound} becomes false if $\max(\varepsilon,\cdot)$ is replaced by $\max(0,\cdot)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\Phi_{m,\eta}(m+\varepsilon)=\max(m,m+\varepsilon-\eta)=m$ since $\varepsilon\le\eta$; the deviation of $u_{n+1}=m+\varepsilon$ from this is exactly $\varepsilon$.
\end{proof}

\section{Many parameters: separability, medians and boxes}

\begin{theorem}[Separability principle]\label{thm:sep}
Let $F_1,\dots,F_d:\R\to\R$ and $\theta\in\R^d$. Then
\[ \Bigl(\forall y\in\R^d:\ \sum_iF_i(\theta_i)\le\sum_iF_i(y_i)\Bigr)\iff\Bigl(\forall i\ \forall t\in\R:\ F_i(\theta_i)\le F_i(t)\Bigr). \]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
($\Rightarrow$) Compare $\theta$ with the vector obtained by replacing the $i$-th coordinate with $t$; all other terms cancel. ($\Leftarrow$) Sum the coordinatewise inequalities.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}
For $k\in\N^d$ and samples $x^{(1)},\dots,x^{(d)}$, set
$L^{\mathrm{sep}}(\theta):=\sum_i L_{2k_i+1}(x^{(i)};\theta_i)$ with coordinatewise median $m_i:=x^{(i)}_{k_i}$, and simultaneous descent $V_\eta(\theta)_i:=\Phi_{m_i,\eta}(\theta_i)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:sepmin}
If each $x^{(i)}$ is sorted up to $2k_i+1$, then $L^{\mathrm{sep}}(m)+\sum_i|\theta_i-m_i|\le L^{\mathrm{sep}}(\theta)$, and $\theta$ minimizes $L^{\mathrm{sep}}$ if and only if $\theta=m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Vector termination time]\label{thm:vecterm}
For $\eta>0$: $V_\eta^{\,n}(\theta)=m$ if and only if $|\theta_i-m_i|\le n\eta$ for all $i$. With $N:=\max_i\lceil|\theta_i-m_i|/\eta\rceil$ we have $V_\eta^{\,N}(\theta)=m$ and $V_\eta^{\,n}(\theta)\ne m$ for all $n<N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}
For even samples, $L^{\mathrm{box}}(\theta):=\sum_i L_{2k_i+2}(x^{(i)};\theta_i)$, with corners $\ell_i:=x^{(i)}_{k_i}$, $h_i:=x^{(i)}_{k_i+1}$ and simultaneous interval update $B_\eta(\theta)_i:=S_{\ell_i,h_i,\eta}(\theta_i)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The minimizer set is a box]\label{thm:box}
If each $x^{(i)}$ is sorted up to $2k_i+2$, then $\theta$ minimizes $L^{\mathrm{box}}$ if and only if $\theta\in\prod_{i=1}^d[\ell_i,h_i]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Theorem~\ref{thm:sep} reduces global minimality to coordinatewise minimality; Theorem~\ref{thm:evenmin} identifies each coordinate's minimizer set.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Box descent terminates at the projection]\label{thm:boxterm}
Let $\eta>0$ and $\ell_i\le h_i$ for all $i$. For every $n\ge\max_i\lceil|\theta_i-\pi_{\ell_i,h_i}(\theta_i)|/\eta\rceil$,
\[ B_\eta^{\,n}(\theta)=\bigl(\pi_{\ell_i,h_i}(\theta_i)\bigr)_{i=1}^{d}, \]
the metric projection of $\theta$ onto the box.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Even-sample vector training theorem]
Under the hypotheses of Theorems~\ref{thm:box} and~\ref{thm:boxterm} there is $N$ such that for all $n\ge N$ the $n$-th iterate of simultaneous clipped descent equals the projection of the initialization onto the minimizer box and is an exact minimizer of $L^{\mathrm{box}}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{example}
Two coordinates with four-point samples $(-3,-1,2,5)$ and $(0,1,1,4)$ give the minimizer box $[-1,2]\times[1,1]$: a segment times a point.
\end{example}

\section{Exact ReLU width of the training step}

\begin{definition}[Width-$k$ network with affine skip]
For $a,b,c\in\R^k$ and $p,q\in\R$,
\[ N_{a,b,c,p,q}(x):=\sum_{j=1}^{k}a_j\relu(b_jx+c_j)+px+q. \]
\end{definition}

The skip term is included deliberately: lower bounds surviving it are strictly stronger.

\begin{lemma}[A rectified unit is flat off its kink]\label{lem:flat}
If $|v|\le|u|$ then $\relu(u+v)+\relu(u-v)-2\relu(u)=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Networks are affine off all kinks]\label{thm:affoff}
Let $h\ge0$ and suppose $|b_j|h\le|b_jx+c_j|$ for every $j$. Then $N(x+h)+N(x-h)-2N(x)=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Kink-witness principle]\label{cor:kink}
If $h\ge0$ and $N(x+h)+N(x-h)-2N(x)\ne0$, then some unit $j$ satisfies $|b_jx+c_j|<|b_j|h$, i.e. its kink lies strictly inside $(x-h,x+h)$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Window separation]\label{lem:sep}
If one unit has its kink inside the radius-$h$ windows at both $x$ and $y$, then $|x-y|<2h$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
From $|bx+c|<|b|h$ we get $b\ne0$; then $|b||x-y|=|(bx+c)-(by+c)|\le|bx+c|+|by+c|<2|b|h$.
\end{proof}

Corollary~\ref{cor:kink} with Lemma~\ref{lem:sep} gives the method: exhibit $r$ points, pairwise at least $2h$ apart, at which the target has nonvanishing radius-$h$ second difference; conclude width $\ge r$.

\begin{theorem}[Scalar update: lower bound two]\label{thm:w2}
Let $t>0$. If $N_{a,b,c,p,q}=\Phi_{m,t}$ on $\R$, then $k\ge2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Take $h=t/2$. At $x=m-t$ the values at $x-h,x,x+h$ are $m-h,m,m$, second difference $-h\ne0$; at $x=m+t$ they are $m,m,m+h$, second difference $h\ne0$. The centers are $2t\ge2h$ apart, so the witnesses are distinct.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Two units suffice]\label{thm:w2suff}
For $t\ge0$ and all $x$: $\ \Phi_{m,t}(x)=m+\relu(x-m-t)-\relu(m-x-t)$; equivalently $\Phi_{m,t}=N_{a,b,c,0,m}$ with $a=(1,-1)$, $b=(1,-1)$, $c=(-(m+t),\,m-t)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}
A weaker argument also shows that no \emph{single} unit $x\mapsto a\relu(bx+c)+e$ can represent $\Phi_{m,t}$ for $t>0$: such a unit is convex ($a\ge0$) or concave ($a\le0$), while $\Phi_{m,t}$ rises, is flat on $[m-t,m+t]$, and rises again. Midpoint convexity of $\relu$ contradicts the sampled values at $m-2t,m-t,m$ in the convex case and at $m,m+t,m+2t$ in the concave case. Unlike the curvature method, this argument does not survive the addition of a skip term.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Explicit four-unit form of the interval update]\label{thm:w4form}
For $\ell\le h$, $\eta\ge0$, and all $\theta$,
\[ S_{\ell,h,\eta}(\theta)=\theta+\eta-\relu\bigl(\theta-(\ell-\eta)\bigr)+\relu(\theta-\ell)-\relu(\theta-h)+\relu\bigl(\theta-(h+\eta)\bigr). \]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Five regions delimited by $\ell-\eta<\ell\le h<h+\eta$. On each, evaluate the update through its piecewise form ($\min(\ell,\theta+\eta)$ left of $\ell$, identity on $[\ell,h]$, $\max(h,\theta-\eta)$ right of $h$) and each rectification as $0$ or its argument; each identity is then polynomial.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Interval update: lower bound four]\label{thm:w4}
Let $\ell<h$ and $\eta>0$. If $N_{a,b,c,p,q}=S_{\ell,h,\eta}$ on $\R$, then $k\ge4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Take $h_0:=\min(\eta,h-\ell)/2>0$, so consecutive kinks among $\ell-\eta<\ell<h<h+\eta$ are at least $2h_0$ apart. The radius-$h_0$ second differences of $S$ at these four centers are $+h_0,+h_0,-h_0,+h_0$ respectively, all nonzero, yielding four witnesses that are pairwise distinct by Lemma~\ref{lem:sep}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact width four]\label{thm:w4exact}
For $\ell<h$ and $\eta>0$, four units with an affine skip realize $S_{\ell,h,\eta}$ exactly (Theorem~\ref{thm:w4form}, with $a=(-1,1,-1,1)$, $b=(1,1,1,1)$, $c=(\eta-\ell,-\ell,-h,-(h+\eta))$, $p=1$, $q=\eta$), and no narrower network can.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:degen}
$S_{m,m,\eta}=\Phi_{m,\eta}$: a degenerate interval reproduces the scalar clipped update.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Width dichotomy]\label{thm:dich}
Let $\ell\le h$ and $\eta>0$. One clipped descent step toward the tropical $L^1$ minimizer set $[\ell,h]$ has exact rectified width, with an arbitrary affine skip permitted,
\[
\mathrm{width}\bigl(S_{\ell,h,\eta}\bigr)=
\begin{cases}
2, & \ell=h \quad(\text{minimizer set is a point}),\\
4, & \ell<h \quad(\text{minimizer set is a nondegenerate segment}).
\end{cases}
\]
\end{theorem}

Since sample parity decides whether the minimizer set is a point or a segment (Corollary~\ref{cor:oddunique} versus Theorem~\ref{thm:evenmin}), Theorem~\ref{thm:dich} says the minimal architecture implementing one training step detects the parity structure of the data.

\section{Algorithms}

\begin{algorithmbox}[Exact tropical training, odd samples]
Given sorted reduced samples $x_0\le\cdots\le x_{2k}$, initialization $\theta_0$ and step $\eta>0$: set $m:=x_k$ and $N:=\lceil|\theta_0-m|/\eta\rceil$; return $(m,N)$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:stop} this is exactly the iteration's output at exactly the step it is produced. Cost $O(n)$ after sorting.
\end{algorithmbox}

\begin{algorithmbox}[Exact tropical training, even samples and boxes]
Given per-coordinate sorted samples of even sizes $2k_i+2$: set $\ell_i:=x^{(i)}_{k_i}$, $h_i:=x^{(i)}_{k_i+1}$; return the box $\prod_i[\ell_i,h_i]$, the projection $\theta^\star_i=\max(\ell_i,\min(h_i,\theta_{0,i}))$, and $N=\max_i\lceil|\theta_{0,i}-\theta^\star_i|/\eta\rceil$. Justified by Theorems~\ref{thm:box}--\ref{thm:boxterm}.
\end{algorithmbox}

\begin{algorithmbox}[Width-optimal compilation of a training step]
Given $\ell\le h$ and $\eta>0$: if $\ell=h$ emit the two-unit network of Theorem~\ref{thm:w2suff}; else emit the four-unit network of Theorem~\ref{thm:w4form}. By Theorem~\ref{thm:dich} the emitted width is minimal.
\end{algorithmbox}

\section{Discussion}

\emph{Why everything is exact.} Three facts conspire. The loss is piecewise affine with integer slopes given by block imbalances (Theorems~\ref{thm:right}--\ref{thm:slab}), so its minimizer set is a face of a subdivision: a vertex in the odd case, an edge in the even case. The clipped update is a genuine one-parameter semigroup (Proposition~\ref{prop:semi}), so iteration is time reparametrization rather than approximation, with no step-size restriction. The distance law is an identity (Proposition~\ref{prop:dist}) rather than a contraction estimate, which is why the upper and matching lower bounds on the stopping time both come out for free.

\emph{Comparison with classical subgradient theory.} For a general convex nonsmooth objective, fixed-step subgradient descent converges only to an $O(\eta)$-neighbourhood, with an $O(1/\sqrt{n})$ rate in function value. Here clipping makes the optimum an exact fixed point and the theory delivers finite termination at an exact optimum for every positive step. Theorem~\ref{thm:sharp} shows this is exactly as fragile as expected and no more: under $\varepsilon$-noise the guarantee degrades to a terminal radius of exactly $\varepsilon$ at effective speed exactly $\eta-\varepsilon$.

\emph{The role of parity.} Sample parity determines whether the argmin is $0$- or $1$-dimensional, whether the terminal parameter is initialization-independent or initialization-selected, and, via Theorem~\ref{thm:dich}, the exact width of the smallest network computing the training step.

\emph{Kink counting as a width method.} Corollary~\ref{cor:kink} with Lemma~\ref{lem:sep} is a general lower-bound technique for shallow rectified networks representing a CPL map: $r$ pairwise $2h$-separated points with nonvanishing radius-$h$ second difference force width $\ge r$. It is immune to affine skips and requires no global shape hypothesis; the two instances proved here, $r=2$ and $r=4$, are the two smallest, and both are tight.

\section{Future directions}

\begin{conjecture}[Width equals the number of curvature sites]
If $f:\R\to\R$ is continuous piecewise linear with exactly $r$ kinks, then the minimal $k$ with $f=N_{a,b,c,p,q}$ for some parameters is exactly $r$.
\end{conjecture}

The kink-witness principle already converts a nonvanishing second difference into a distinct unit whenever the test windows are disjoint, so the lower bound needs no convexity, differentiability, or sign pattern; the matching upper bound should follow from the telescoping construction of Theorem~\ref{thm:w4form}.

\begin{conjecture}[Tropical width spectrum of box descent]
For the separable box update on $d$ coordinates with $s:=\#\{i:\ell_i<h_i\}$ nondegenerate coordinates, the total rectified width required to implement one simultaneous step as a map $\R^d\to\R^d$ from scalar units with arbitrary affine skips is exactly $2d+2s$.
\end{conjecture}

Separability makes the curvature test coordinatewise, so widths should add: $2$ per degenerate coordinate, $4$ per nondegenerate one.

\begin{conjecture}[Sharp asymptotic perturbation radius]
For every $0\le\varepsilon<\eta$ and every $\varepsilon$-perturbed trajectory, $\limsup_n|u_n-m|\le\varepsilon$, and the supremum of $\limsup_n|u_n-m|$ over trajectories equals $\varepsilon$; moreover $\limsup_n\bigl(L(u_n)-L(m)\bigr)=n_{\text{samples}}\cdot\varepsilon$ for a sample whose median has full one-sided multiplicity.
\end{conjecture}

Further directions include the general odd-sample statement for every $\eta>0$; separable $d$-parameter tropical affine models with coordinatewise three-point losses, where simultaneous clipped descent should terminate in the maximum of the coordinatewise times; the quantitative perturbed limit $\max\bigl(0,|\theta_0-m|-n(\eta-\varepsilon)\bigr)$ valid until the trajectory enters the closed $\varepsilon$-neighbourhood; and the behaviour of the even-sample minimizer interval under sampling noise, in particular the induced distribution of the terminal point on the optimal face.

\section{Conclusion}

For tropical $L^1$ regression, training is not an approximation process. A single counting inequality determines the whole minimizer geometry: a point for odd samples, a segment for even ones, a product box in the separable multi-parameter setting. A semigroup identity turns iterated clipped subgradient descent into an exactly solvable flow, giving finite termination with a stopping time that is simultaneously an upper and a lower bound. Noise degrades this in a fully quantified way with an attained saturation radius. And the same piecewise-linear rigidity makes the architecture of the update rule an invariant: exactly two rectified units when the optimum is a point, exactly four when it is a segment.

  "demo": """"
Exact training dynamics of tropical L1 regression -- numerical demonstrations.

This self-contained script demonstrates, by direct computation, every headline
result of the accompanying paper:

  1. Tropical L1 loss and the counting (block-imbalance) growth mechanism.
  2. Odd samples: unique median minimizer, growth bound L(m) + |t-m| <= L(t),
     exact affine slabs.
  3. The clipped update: semigroup law, exact distance law, iterate = flow.
  4. Finite termination at exactly ceil(|x0 - m| / eta) steps, and no earlier.
  5. Even samples: the minimizer set is exactly the central closed interval;
     interval descent conserves the metric projection and halts on it.
  6. Perturbed descent: the bound max(eps, |u0-m| - n(eta-eps)) and the
     attained saturation radius eps.
  7. Separable multi-parameter models: coordinatewise medians, and the
     even-sample minimizer BOX; termination in max_i of coordinate times.
  8. Exact ReLU widths: 2 units realize the scalar clipped update, 4 units
     realize the interval update, and the discrete curvature test detects
     the corresponding numbers of kinks.

Run with:  python3 demo.py
No dependencies beyond the Python standard library.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from typing import Callable, List, Sequence, Tuple

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Tropical L1 loss
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def l1_loss(xs: Sequence[float], theta: float) -> float:
    """Tropical L1 empirical loss L(theta) = sum_i |theta - x_i|."""
    return sum(abs(theta - x) for x in xs)


def block_imbalance(xs: Sequence[float], pivot: float) -> int:
    """(# samples <= pivot) - (# samples > pivot): the local growth rate to the right."""
    low = sum(1 for x in xs if x <= pivot)
    return low - (len(xs) - low)


def median_lo_hi(xs: Sequence[float]) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Endpoints [lo, hi] of the exact minimizer set of the tropical L1 loss.

    Odd size 2k+1 -> lo = hi = x_k (a point).
    Even size 2k+2 -> [x_k, x_{k+1}] (a segment, possibly degenerate).
    """
    s = sorted(xs)
    n = len(s)
    if n % 2 == 1:
        k = (n - 1) // 2
        return s[k], s[k]
    k = n // 2 - 1
    return s[k], s[k + 1]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. The clipped tropical update (the flow) and interval descent
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def tropical_flow(m: float, t: float, x: float) -> float:
    """Clipped update: move x by t toward m, stopping at m."""
    if x < m:
        return min(m, x + t)
    return max(m, x - t)


def proj_icc(lo: float, hi: float, theta: float) -> float:
    """Metric projection of theta onto [lo, hi]."""
    return max(lo, min(hi, theta))


def interval_step(lo: float, hi: float, eta: float, theta: float) -> float:
    """One clipped subgradient step of size eta toward the interval [lo, hi]."""
    return tropical_flow(proj_icc(lo, hi, theta), eta, theta)


def iterate(f: Callable[[float], float], n: int, x: float) -> float:
    """n-fold iterate of a scalar map."""
    for _ in range(n):
        x = f(x)
    return x


def stopping_time(x0: float, target: float, eta: float) -> int:
    """Exact number of clipped steps of size eta needed to reach the target."""
    return math.ceil(abs(x0 - target) / eta)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. ReLU networks
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def relu(x: float) -> float:
    return max(x, 0.0)


def relu_net(
    a: Sequence[float], b: Sequence[float], c: Sequence[float], p: float, q: float, x: float
) -> float:
    """Width-k rectified network with an affine skip: sum_j a_j relu(b_j x + c_j) + p x + q."""
    return sum(aj * relu(bj * x + cj) for aj, bj, cj in zip(a, b, c)) + p * x + q


def second_difference(f: Callable[[float], float], x: float, h: float) -> float:
    """Discrete curvature test D_h f(x) = f(x+h) + f(x-h) - 2 f(x)."""
    return f(x + h) + f(x - h) - 2.0 * f(x)


def count_curvature_sites(
    f: Callable[[float], float], lo: float, hi: float, h: float, tol: float = 1e-9
) -> int:
    """Count well-separated points in [lo, hi] with nonvanishing radius-h curvature.

    Sites closer than 2h are merged, matching the window-separation lemma: two
    windows of radius h that share a rectified unit must have centers < 2h apart.
    """
    grid = [lo + i * (hi - lo) / 4000.0 for i in range(4001)]
    hits = [x for x in grid if abs(second_difference(f, x, h)) > tol]
    sites: List[float] = []
    for x in hits:

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from typing import Callable, List, Sequence, Tuple

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Tropical L1 loss
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def l1_loss(xs: Sequence[float], theta: float) -> float:
    """Tropical L1 empirical loss L(theta) = sum_i |theta - x_i|."""
    return sum(abs(theta - x) for x in xs)


def block_imbalance(xs: Sequence[float], pivot: float) -> int:
    """(# samples <= pivot) - (# samples > pivot): the local growth rate to the right."""
    low = sum(1 for x in xs if x <= pivot)
    return low - (len(xs) - low)


def median_lo_hi(xs: Sequence[float]) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Endpoints [lo, hi] of the exact minimizer set of the tropical L1 loss.

    Odd size 2k+1 -> lo = hi = x_k (a point).
    Even size 2k+2 -> [x_k, x_{k+1}] (a segment, possibly degenerate).
    """
    s = sorted(xs)
    n = len(s)
    if n % 2 == 1:
        k = (n - 1) // 2
        return s[k], s[k]
    k = n // 2 - 1
    return s[k], s[k + 1]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. The clipped tropical update (the flow) and interval descent
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def tropical_flow(m: float, t: float, x: float) -> float:
    """Clipped update: move x by t toward m, stopping at m."""
    if x < m:
        return min(m, x + t)
    return max(m, x - t)


def proj_icc(lo: float, hi: float, theta: float) -> float:
    """Metric projection of theta onto [lo, hi]."""
    return max(lo, min(hi, theta))


def interval_step(lo: float, hi: float, eta: float, theta: float) -> float:
    """One clipped subgradient step of size eta toward the interval [lo, hi]."""
    return tropical_flow(proj_icc(lo, hi, theta), eta, theta)


def iterate(f: Callable[[float], float], n: int, x: float) -> float:
    """n-fold iterate of a scalar map."""
    for _ in range(n):
        x = f(x)
    return x


def stopping_time(x0: float, target: float, eta: float) -> int:
    """Exact number of clipped steps of size eta needed to reach the target."""
    return math.ceil(abs(x0 - target) / eta)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. ReLU networks
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def relu(x: float) -> float:
    return max(x, 0.0)


def relu_net(
    a: Sequence[float], b: Sequence[float], c: Sequence[float], p: float, q: float, x: float
) -> float:
    """Width-k rectified network with an affine skip: sum_j a_j relu(b_j x + c_j) + p x + q."""
    return sum(aj * relu(bj * x + cj) for aj, bj, cj in zip(a, b, c)) + p * x + q


def second_difference(f: Callable[[float], float], x: float, h: float) -> float:
    """Discrete curvature test D_h f(x) = f(x+h) + f(x-h) - 2 f(x)."""
    return f(x + h) + f(x - h) - 2.0 * f(x)


def count_curvature_sites(
    f: Callable[[float], float], lo: float, hi: float, h: float, tol: float = 1e-9
) -> int:
    """Count well-separated points in [lo, hi] with nonvanishing radius-h curvature.

    Sites closer than 2h are merged, matching the window-separation lemma: two
    windows of radius h that share a rectified unit must have centers < 2h apart.
    """
    grid = [lo + i * (hi - lo) / 4000.0 for i in range(4001)]
    hits = [x for x in grid if abs(second_difference(f, x, h)) > tol]
    sites: List[float] = []
    for x in hits:
        if not sites or x - sites[-1] >= 2.0 * h:
            sites.append(x)
    return len(sites)

import random
from typing import Callable, List, Sequence, Tuple

TOL = 1e-9


def l1(xs: Sequence[float], t: float) -> float:
    return float(sum(abs(t - x) for x in xs))


def minset(xs: Sequence[float]) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    s = sorted(xs)
    n = len(s)
    if n % 2 == 1:
        k = (n - 1) // 2
        return s[k], s[k]
    k = n // 2 - 1
    return s[k], s[k + 1]


def proj(lo: float, hi: float, t: float) -> float:
    return max(lo, min(hi, t))


def flow(m: float, t: float, x: float) -> float:
    return min(m, x + t) if x < m else max(m, x - t)


def istep(lo: float, hi: float, eta: float, t: float) -> float:
    return flow(proj(lo, hi, t), eta, t)


def iterate(f: Callable[[float], float], n: int, x: float) -> float:
    for _ in range(n):
        x = f(x)
    return x


def relu(x: float) -> float:
    return max(x, 0.0)


def rand_sample(n: int) -> List[float]:
    return sorted(round(random.uniform(-10, 10), 3) for _ in range(n))

    fails = {f"T{i}": 0 for i in range(1, 10)}

            bound = n * max(0.0, abs(th0 - target) - k * eta)
            if excess < -TOL or excess > bound + 1e-8:

        eps = round(random.uniform(0, 1) * eta, 4)
        u, u0 = th0, th0

        coords = [rand_sample(2 * random.randint(1, 3)) for _ in range(d)]

        start = [random.uniform(-14, 14) for _ in range(d)]

        times = [math.ceil(abs(s0 - g) / eta) for s0, g in zip(start, tgt)]

        if any(abs(z - g) > 1e-9 for z, g in zip(theta, tgt)):
            fails["T8"] += 1
        best = sum(l1(c, g) for c, g in zip(coords, tgt))
        for _ in range(20):

        mm = random.uniform(-5, 5)

    def sites(f: Callable[[float], float], a: float, b: float, h: float) -> int:

        x = a

    n2 = sites(lambda z: flow(0.0, 1.0, z), -6, 6, 0.5)

    print(f"  curvature sites: point optimum -> {n2} (expect 2), segment optimum -> {n4} (expect 4)")

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import List, NamedTuple, Sequence, Tuple


class TrainingCertificate(NamedTuple):
    minimizer_lo: float          # lower endpoint of the exact minimizer set
    minimizer_hi: float          # upper endpoint (equal to lo when the sample size is odd)
    terminal_parameter: float    # the parameter clipped descent halts at
    stopping_time: int           # exact number of steps; no earlier iterate is optimal
    optimal_loss: float          # empirical risk at the optimum
    geometry: str                # "point" or "segment"
    relu_width_of_step: int      # exact rectified width of one descent step: 2 or 4


def l1_loss(samples: Sequence[float], theta: float) -> float:
    """Tropical L1 empirical loss sum_i |theta - x_i|."""
    return float(sum(abs(theta - x) for x in samples))


def minimizer_interval(samples: Sequence[float]) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Exact minimizer set [lo, hi] of the tropical L1 loss.

    Odd size 2k+1: the single point x_(k). Even size 2k+2: the closed interval
    between the two central order statistics.
    """
    s: List[float] = sorted(samples)
    n = len(s)
    if n == 0:
        raise ValueError("empty sample")
    if n % 2 == 1:
        k = (n - 1) // 2
        return s[k], s[k]
    k = n // 2 - 1
    return s[k], s[k + 1]


def train_tropical_l1(
    samples: Sequence[float], theta0: float, eta: float
) -> TrainingCertificate:
    """Solve the training run in closed form, without iterating.

    The clipped update forms a one-parameter semigroup, so n steps of size eta
    equal one flow of duration n*eta, and the distance obeys the exact identity
    max(0, |theta0 - target| - n*eta). Hence the run terminates precisely at
    ceil(|theta0 - target| / eta) steps and never earlier.
    """
    if eta <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("step size must be positive")
    lo, hi = minimizer_interval(samples)
    target = max(lo, min(hi, theta0))              # metric projection onto the optimum
    steps = math.ceil(abs(theta0 - target) / eta)
    return TrainingCertificate(
        minimizer_lo=lo,
        minimizer_hi=hi,
        terminal_parameter=target,
        stopping_time=steps,
        optimal_loss=l1_loss(samples, target),
        geometry="point" if lo == hi else "segment",
        relu_width_of_step=2 if lo == hi else 4,
    )

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import List, NamedTuple, Sequence


class ReluProgram(NamedTuple):
    a: List[float]     # output weights
    b: List[float]     # input weights
    c: List[float]     # biases
    p: float           # affine skip slope
    q: float           # affine skip offset
    width: int         # number of rectified units; provably minimal
    regime: str        # "point optimum" or "segment optimum"


def relu(x: float) -> float:
    return max(x, 0.0)


def relu_net(prog: ReluProgram, x: float) -> float:
    """Evaluate sum_j a_j relu(b_j x + c_j) + p x + q."""
    return sum(aj * relu(bj * x + cj) for aj, bj, cj in zip(prog.a, prog.b, prog.c)) + prog.p * x + prog.q


def compile_descent_step(lo: float, hi: float, eta: float) -> ReluProgram:
    """Emit the narrowest rectified network computing one clipped step toward [lo, hi].

    Degenerate interval (lo == hi = m), two units:
        m + relu(x - m - eta) - relu(m - x - eta).
    Nondegenerate interval, four units with a unit-slope skip:
        x + eta - relu(x-(lo-eta)) + relu(x-lo) - relu(x-hi) + relu(x-(hi+eta)).
    Both widths are minimal, even allowing an arbitrary affine skip, because the
    maps have respectively 2 and 4 pairwise separated kinks.
    """
    if lo > hi:
        raise ValueError("empty interval")
    if eta <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("step size must be positive")
    if lo == hi:
        m = lo
        return ReluProgram(a=[1.0, -1.0], b=[1.0, -1.0], c=[-(m + eta), m - eta],
                           p=0.0, q=m, width=2, regime="point optimum")
    return ReluProgram(a=[-1.0, 1.0, -1.0, 1.0], b=[1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0],
                       c=[eta - lo, -lo, -hi, -(hi + eta)],
                       p=1.0, q=eta, width=4, regime="segment optimum")


def max_compilation_error(lo: float, hi: float, eta: float, samples: int = 2001) -> float:
    """Sup-norm error of the emitted program against the true update, on a wide grid."""
    prog = compile_descent_step(lo, hi, eta)
    span_lo, span_hi = lo - 5.0 * eta - 3.0, hi + 5.0 * eta + 3.0

    def true_step(x: float) -> float:
        target = max(lo, min(hi, x))
        return min(target, x + eta) if x < target else max(target, x - eta)

    grid: Sequence[float] = [span_lo + i * (span_hi - span_lo) / (samples - 1) for i in range(samples)]
    return max(abs(relu_net(prog, x) - true_step(x)) for x in grid)

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable, List, NamedTuple


class WidthCertificate(NamedTuple):
    witnesses: List[float]   # pairwise 2h-separated probe centers with nonzero curvature
    radius: float            # the common window radius h
    lower_bound: int         # any network representing f, with an affine skip, needs this width


def second_difference(f: Callable[[float], float], x: float, h: float) -> float:
    """Discrete curvature D_h f(x) = f(x+h) + f(x-h) - 2 f(x)."""
    return f(x + h) + f(x - h) - 2.0 * f(x)


def width_lower_bound(
    f: Callable[[float], float],
    lo: float,
    hi: float,
    radius: float,
    resolution: int = 20000,
    tol: float = 1e-9,
) -> WidthCertificate:
    """Certify a width lower bound for any rectified network with an affine skip computing f.

    Mechanism. A single unit x -> a*relu(b x + c) is affine on any window that
    misses its kink, so its second difference there vanishes; an affine skip has
    vanishing second difference everywhere. Hence a nonzero reading D_h f(x) != 0
    forces some unit to have its kink strictly inside (x-h, x+h). Two windows of
    radius h that share a unit must have centers less than 2h apart, so probes
    that are pairwise at least 2h apart need pairwise distinct units.

    Complexity: O(resolution) evaluations of f; the greedy sweep keeps the first
    probe of each 2h-separated cluster, which is exactly the separation condition.
    """
    witnesses: List[float] = []
    last = float("-inf")
    for i in range(resolution + 1):
        x = lo + i * (hi - lo) / resolution
        if abs(second_difference(f, x, radius)) > tol and x - last >= 2.0 * radius:
            witnesses.append(x)
            last = x
    return WidthCertificate(witnesses=witnesses, radius=radius, lower_bound=len(witnesses))

const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
const cv = $('lossCanvas'), ctx = cv.getContext('2d');

let xs = [-3,-1,0,4,9], theta = 11, steps = 0, timer = null, path = [];

function parseSamples(){

  $('cur').textContent = theta.toFixed(4);

function draw(){

  const xmax=Math.max(...a, theta, parseFloat($('th0').value))+3;

  const span=ymax-ymin||1; ymin-=0.12*span; ymax+=0.10*span;
  const X=t=>pad+(t-xmin)/(xmax-xmin)*(W-2*pad);
  const Y=v=>H-pad-(v-ymin)/(ymax-ymin)*(H-2*pad);

  // grid
  ctx.strokeStyle='#e6ecf4'; ctx.lineWidth=2;

    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x,pad); ctx.lineTo(x,H-pad); ctx.stroke(); }
  for(let i=0;i<=6;i++){ const y=pad+i*(H-2*pad)/6;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(pad,y); ctx.lineTo(W-pad,y); ctx.stroke(); }

  // minimizer set
  ctx.fillStyle='rgba(46,125,50,.16)';
  if(hi>lo) ctx.fillRect(X(lo),pad,X(hi)-X(lo),H-2*pad);
  else { ctx.strokeStyle='#2e7d32'; ctx.lineWidth=4;
         ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(X(lo),pad); ctx.lineTo(X(lo),H-pad); ctx.stroke(); }

  // growth envelope
  ctx.strokeStyle='#c62828'; ctx.lineWidth=3; ctx.setLineDash([9,7]); ctx.beginPath();
  const base=loss(a,lo), slope=(hi>lo)?2:1;
  for(let i=0;i<=600;i++){ const t=xmin+i*(xmax-xmin)/600;
    const d = (t<lo)?(lo-t):((t>hi)?(t-hi):0);
    const v = base + slope*d;
    (i? ctx.lineTo(X(t),Y(v)) : ctx.moveTo(X(t),Y(v))); }
  ctx.stroke(); ctx.setLineDash([]);

  // loss curve
  ctx.strokeStyle='#1f4e79'; ctx.lineWidth=5; ctx.beginPath();
  for(let i=0;i<=1200;i++){ const t=xmin+i*(xmax-xmin)/1200;
    (i? ctx.lineTo(X(t),Y(loss(a,t))) : ctx.moveTo(X(t),Y(loss(a,t)))); }
  ctx.stroke();

  // sample points
  ctx.fillStyle='#1f4e79';
  a.forEach(x=>{ ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(X(x),Y(loss(a,x)),7,0,7); ctx.fill(); });

  // trajectory
  ctx.strokeStyle='#ef6c00'; ctx.lineWidth=3;
  path.forEach((p,i)=>{
    ctx.fillStyle='#ef6c00';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(X(p),Y(loss(a,p)),6,0,7); ctx.fill();
    if(i>0){ ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(X(path[i-1]),Y(loss(a,path[i-1])));
             ctx.lineTo(X(p),Y(loss(a,p))); ctx.stroke(); }
  });
  // current point
  ctx.fillStyle='#6a1b9a';
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(X(theta),Y(loss(a,theta)),10,0,7); ctx.fill();

  ctx.fillStyle='#5d7085'; ctx.font='24px -apple-system,Segoe UI,Roboto,sans-serif';
  ctx.fillText('θ', W/2, H-18);
  ctx.save(); ctx.translate(20,H/2); ctx.rotate(-Math.PI/2);
  ctx.fillText('empirical risk', -60, 0); ctx.restore();
  ctx.fillStyle='#12243a'; ctx.font='bold 26px -apple-system,Segoe UI,Roboto,sans-serif';
  ctx.fillText(`η = ${eta.toFixed(2)}   step ${steps}`, pad+8, pad-20);
}

function reset(){
  clearInterval(timer); timer=null;
  xs=parseSamples(); theta=parseFloat($('th0').value); steps=0; path=[theta];
  refreshReadout(); draw();
}
function doStep(){
  const eta=parseFloat($('eta').value), eps=parseFloat($('eps').value);
  theta=step1(xs,eta,eps,theta); steps++; path.push(theta);
  if(path.length>400) path.shift();
  refreshReadout(); draw();

$('btnRun').onclick=()=>{ if(timer){clearInterval(timer);timer=null;return;}

    if(parseFloat($('eps').value)===0 && theta===proj(lo,hi,theta)){clearInterval(timer);timer=null;}
    if(steps>300){clearInterval(timer);timer=null;} },260); };
$('btnReset').onclick=reset;
$('btnOdd').onclick=()=>{ $('samples').value='-3, -1, 0, 4, 9'; reset(); };
$('btnEven').onclick=()=>{ $('samples').value='-3, -1, 2, 5'; reset(); };
['eta','th0','eps'].forEach(id=>$(id).oninput=()=>{
  $('etaV').textContent=parseFloat($('eta').value).toFixed(2);
  $('th0V').textContent=parseFloat($('th0').value).toFixed(1);
  $('epsV').textContent=parseFloat($('eps').value).toFixed(2);
  reset(); });
$('samples').oninput=reset;
reset();
</script>
</body>
</html>

  <h1>Kink Counting: how many rectified units does one training step need?</h1>
  <p class="sub">One clipped descent step is a continuous piecewise-linear map, so it <em>is</em> a small
  rectified network. To find the smallest one, probe the map with the discrete curvature test
  \(D_h f(x)=f(x+h)+f(x-h)-2f(x)\). A single unit is affine on any window missing its kink, and a linear
  bypass never contributes — so a nonzero reading <strong>forces</strong> a unit with its kink inside the window.
  Drag the probe, shrink the window, and count.</p>

  <div class="grid">
    <div class="panel">
      <canvas id="cv" width="1400" height="660"></canvas>
      <div class="note" style="margin-top:8px">Top: the update map (thick) with its kinks marked. The purple band is

        <tr><td class="k">separated curvature sites</td><td class="v big" id="sites">—</td></tr>
        <tr><td class="k">forced width (lower bound)</td><td class="v big" id="lb">—</td></tr>

        difference, on a window missing its kink; the affine skip always has vanishing second difference.

        \(x\) and \(y\), then \(|x-y|<2h\). Proof: \(|b||x-y|=|(bx+c)-(by+c)|\le|bx+c|+|by+c|<2|b|h\).

  "interactive_layout": "# When Training Stops: Tropical $L^1$ Regression, End to End

> **What you will learn.** How replacing ordinary arithmetic with $\max$ and $+$ turns a training problem into a
> counting problem; why the resulting optimizer *terminates* instead of merely converging; how noise degrades
> that guarantee by exactly the amount you would guess and no more; and why the smallest neural network that can
> execute one training step tells you whether the optimum is a point or a segment.

---

## 1. Two operations, one geometry

In [tropical arithmetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_geometry) we set

$$a \oplus b = \max(a,b), \qquad a \otimes b = a + b.$$

Every tropical polynomial is a maximum of affine functions, hence convex and piecewise linear; every difference
of two tropical polynomials is a general continuous piecewise-linear map. That is exactly the class computed by
networks whose only nonlinearity is $\mathrm{relu}(x)=\max(x,0)$ — the [rectifier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rectifier_(neural_networks)).
Tropical algebra and rectified networks are two dialects for one geometry.

Take the simplest tropical model with a trainable parameter,
$$z \;\longmapsto\; z\otimes\theta \;=\; z+\theta .$$
Given data $(z_j,y_j)$ and absolute-error loss, the $j$-th residual is $|\theta - x_j|$ where $x_j := y_j-z_j$.
So the whole model reduces to one question about $n$ numbers:

$$\text{minimize}\quad L(\theta)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\bigl|\theta - x_i\bigr|.$$

<details>
<summary><strong>Background: why absolute error and not squared error?</strong></summary>

Squared error gives the mean, which is smooth and unique but not robust. Absolute error gives the median: robust
to outliers, and — as we are about to see — *piecewise linear*, which is precisely what makes the tropical
structure visible. The loss is a sum of $n$ V-shaped functions, so it is convex, piecewise affine, and its slope
changes by $+2$ each time $\theta$ crosses a data point.
</details>

---

## 2. The counting mechanism

Everything follows from one observation. Slide $\theta$ rightward from a pivot $p$. Each sample at or below $p$
contributes a term that grows by exactly the displacement; each sample above contributes a term that shrinks by
at most the displacement. So, with $j$ samples at or below the pivot,

$$L(\theta) \;\ge\; L(p) + \bigl(j-(n-j)\bigr)(\theta-p),$$

and if the move crosses no data point this is an *equality*. The slope of the loss is the **block imbalance**.

Feed the mechanism two pivots and you get the whole minimizer geometry:

- **Odd $n=2k+1$:** at the median $m=x_k$ the imbalance is $1$ in both directions, so
  $L(m)+|\theta-m|\le L(\theta)$ — a strict, uniquely-minimized valley.
- **Even $n=2k+2$:** between the two central order statistics the blocks are balanced and the loss is
  *constant*; outside, the imbalance is $2$. The minimizer set is **exactly** $[x_k,x_{k+1}]$.

{{visualization:0}}

---

## 3. Play with it: the descent laboratory

Now the optimizer. Subgradient descent counts samples; the only refinement that matters is **clipping** — never
overshoot the target:

$$\Phi_{m,t}(x)=\begin{cases}\min(m,x+t), & x<m,\\ \max(m,x-t), & x\ge m.\end{cases}$$

Edit the sample below, set a step size, and run. Watch the predicted stopping time and the observed one agree,
every single time. Then delete one sample point to flip the parity, and watch the optimum turn from a point into
a segment.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

<details>
<summary><strong>Click to reveal why termination is exact, with the two identities that do all the work</strong></summary>

**Semigroup law.** For $s\ge0$, $\ \Phi_{m,s}\circ\Phi_{m,t}=\Phi_{m,t+s}$. Composing clipped steps just adds
their durations, so $n$ steps of size $\eta$ are *literally* one step of size $n\eta$. There is no discretization
error at any step size — the discrete algorithm and the continuous flow coincide.

**Distance law.** $\ \bigl|\Phi_{m,t}(x)-m\bigr| = \max\bigl(0,|x-m|-t\bigr)$. Not an inequality: an identity.

Combining, $\Phi^{\,n}_{m,\eta}(x_0)=m$ **iff** $|x_0-m|\le n\eta$. Hence the stopping time is exactly
$$N=\left\lceil \frac{|x_0-m|}{\eta}\right\rceil,$$
and no earlier iterate is optimal — the ceiling is simultaneously an upper and a lower bound. Because $L$ is
$n$-Lipschitz, the excess risk is squeezed between $0$ and $n\max(0,|x_0-m|-n\eta)$, hitting zero exactly at $N$.

For an even sample the target is the *nearest* optimal point $\pi(\theta)=\max(\ell,\min(h,\theta))$, and the
projection is a conserved quantity of the dynamics: one step never changes which optimum you are aiming at. That
single invariance collapses interval descent to the scalar flow, so training halts at $\pi(\theta_0)$ after
$\lceil|\theta_0-\pi(\theta_0)|/\eta\rceil$ steps. *Where you start decides which optimum you get.*
</details>

---

## 4. Solving the run without running it

Because the dynamics is exactly solvable, training is a closed-form computation: sort, read off the central order
statistics, project, divide, round up.

{{algorithm:0}}

The same reasoning lifts verbatim to many parameters. A separable objective $\sum_i F_i(\theta_i)$ is minimized
exactly when each coordinate is — compare $\theta$ with the vector that differs in one coordinate only — so the
$d$-parameter minimizer set is a **product box** of central segments, and simultaneous descent lands on the
projection of the initialization onto that box after the maximum of the coordinatewise times. The slowest
coordinate sets the clock.

{{algorithm:1}}

## 5. What noise does

Exact termination sounds fragile. It degrades in a completely quantified way. If every update is corrupted by an
error of size at most $\varepsilon\le\eta$, then

$$|u_n-m| \;\le\; \max\bigl(\varepsilon,\ |u_0-m|-n(\eta-\varepsilon)\bigr).$$

Effective speed $\eta-\varepsilon$; saturation radius $\varepsilon$. And the saturation is *not* slack in the
proof: the constant trajectory $u_n\equiv m+\varepsilon$ is a legal perturbed run sitting forever at distance
exactly $\varepsilon$, because the clipped update maps $m+\varepsilon$ to $m$ and the noise puts it straight
back. So replacing $\max(\varepsilon,\cdot)$ by $\max(0,\cdot)$ would make the statement false.

{{visualization:1}}

Try it yourself: return to the laboratory above and raise the noise slider. The run stops terminating and starts
rattling around inside a band — and the band has exactly the radius the theorem predicts.

---

## 6. Reading geometry off architecture

Here is the twist. One clipped descent step is a continuous piecewise-linear map, so it *is* a rectified network.
How narrow can that network be, if we generously allow an affine bypass $px+q$ on top of the units?

The tool is a **discrete curvature test**. For a window of radius $h$ at $x$, form
$$D_h f(x) = f(x+h)+f(x-h)-2f(x).$$
A single unit is affine on any window that misses its kink, and the bypass never contributes — so a nonzero
reading *forces* a unit with its kink strictly inside the window. Add the observation that two windows of radius
$h$ more than $2h$ apart cannot share a unit, and width lower bounds become an act of counting.

Probe the two update maps yourself:

Point optimum, two kinks at $m\pm t$, exact width $2$:
$$\Phi_{m,t}(x) \;=\; m + \mathrm{relu}(x-m-t) - \mathrm{relu}(m-x-t).$$

Segment optimum $[\ell,h]$, four kinks at $\ell-\eta,\ \ell,\ h,\ h+\eta$, exact width $4$:
$$S(\theta) \;=\; \theta+\eta-\mathrm{relu}\bigl(\theta-(\ell-\eta)\bigr)+\mathrm{relu}(\theta-\ell)
-\mathrm{relu}(\theta-h)+\mathrm{relu}\bigl(\theta-(h+\eta)\bigr).$$

Since a degenerate interval $\ell=h$ reproduces the scalar update, both cases live in one family, and we get the
**width dichotomy**: one training step needs exactly $2$ units when the optimum is a point and exactly $4$ when
it is a nondegenerate segment. The width of the optimizer is a faithful invariant of the tropical minimizer
geometry — which is decided by the parity of the sample.
</details>

Three concrete conjectures, all falsifiable, all reachable from what is proved above.

1. **Width equals the number of curvature sites.** For a continuous piecewise-linear $f$ with exactly $r$ kinks,

**The moral.** Tropical arithmetic was invented to turn optimization into algebra. Here the circle closes: an
algebraic model, trained by an ordinary optimizer, produces dynamics so rigid that its convergence, its optimum,
and even the architecture needed to express its own update rule are all determined by counting.

/-!
# Tropical boxes: even samples in `d` parameters

`Tropical.EML.TropicalMedianDescent` shows that for an even scalar sample the
tropical `L¹` minimizer set is a segment, and
`Tropical.EML.TropicalDescentRobustness` handles `d` separable coordinates with odd
samples (a single point).  This file combines the two: for a separable
`d`-parameter tropical affine model with **even** samples in each coordinate the
minimizer set is exactly a *box* — the product of the `d` central segments — and
simultaneous clipped descent reaches the metric projection of the initialization
onto that box, in the maximum of the `d` coordinatewise times.

Main results.

* `sep_minimizes_iff_coordinatewise` : a general separability principle — a
  separable objective is minimized exactly when every coordinate is.
* `box_minimizes_iff_mem_box` : the minimizer set of the separable even-sample
  tropical `L¹` loss is exactly `∏ᵢ [xᵢ(kᵢ), xᵢ(kᵢ+1)]`.
* `boxStep_terminates` : simultaneous clipped descent freezes at the projection of
  the initialization onto the box after finitely many steps.
* `box_descent_reaches_minimizer` : and that projection is an empirical-risk
  minimizer, so training halts at an exact optimum in finite time.
-/
